Let \([XYZ]\) denote the area of \(\triangle XYZ\).

Since \(\triangle ABC\) is equilateral with inradius \(2\), its circumradius is \(4\). The incenter \(I\) is also the circumcenter, so

\[
AI=4.
\]

Also \(AI\) bisects \(\angle A=60^\circ\), hence

\[
\angle BAI=\angle IAC=30^\circ.
\]

For any point \(P\) with \(PI=1\), the segment \(AP\) must meet the circle centered at \(I\) with radius \(1\). The largest possible angle between \(AP\) and \(AI\) occurs when \(AP\) is tangent to that circle.

Let \(\theta\) be this maximum angle, measured toward \(C\). In the right triangle formed by \(A\), \(I\), and the tangency point,

\[
\sin\theta=\frac{1}{AI}=\frac14,
\qquad
\cos\theta=\frac{\sqrt{15}}4.
\]

Now,

\[
[APB]=\frac12(AP)(AB)\sin\angle BAP,
\]
\[
[APC]=\frac12(AP)(AC)\sin\angle PAC.
\]

Because \(AB=AC\),

\[
\frac{[APB]}{[APC]}
=
\frac{\sin\angle BAP}{\sin\angle PAC}.
\]

If \(AP\) makes angle \(\theta\) with \(AI\) toward \(C\), then

\[
\angle BAP=30^\circ+\theta,
\qquad
\angle PAC=30^\circ-\theta.
\]

Thus the ratio is

\[
\frac{\sin(30^\circ+\theta)}{\sin(30^\circ-\theta)}.
\]

This is maximized at the tangent angle \(\theta\), where \(\sin\theta=\frac14\) and \(\cos\theta=\frac{\sqrt{15}}4\). Therefore,

\[
\frac{\sin(30^\circ+\theta)}{\sin(30^\circ-\theta)}
=
\frac{\frac12\cos\theta+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin\theta}
{\frac12\cos\theta-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin\theta}.
\]

Substitute \(\cos\theta=\frac{\sqrt{15}}4\) and \(\sin\theta=\frac14\):

\[
=
\frac{\frac{\sqrt{15}}8+\frac{\sqrt3}{8}}
{\frac{\sqrt{15}}8-\frac{\sqrt3}{8}}
=
\frac{\sqrt{15}+\sqrt3}{\sqrt{15}-\sqrt3}.
\]

Rationalizing,

\[
\frac{\sqrt{15}+\sqrt3}{\sqrt{15}-\sqrt3}
=
\frac{(\sqrt{15}+\sqrt3)^2}{15-3}
=
\frac{18+6\sqrt5}{12}
=
\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}.
\]

Thus the maximum value is

\[
\boxed{\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}}.
\]
